correctness.rationale: For each unit-normalized Hermite window the exact Gaussian ambiguity factor is proved. The weighted squared-channel singular value is \(F_w(s)\). Its derivative has zero or two stationary radii; one is a strict local minimum. For \(T>2\) the boundary margin strictly increases while the interior margin strictly decreases, and their endpoint inequalities force a unique crossing. The implicit equation, all threshold cases and asymptotic are algebraic consequences. Independent quadrature, symbolic and scalar optimization checks passed; these finite tests do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The exact diskwise maximin weight, its threshold T=2, the entire optimizer set at threshold, and the unique transcendental equioscillation branch above threshold were not identified in inspected full-text primary Hermite STFT studies or indexed published results. Prior publications supply the Laguerre ambiguity identity and qualitative multiwindow strategy, not this sharp optimized two-channel statement. This is a best-evidence comparison, not an assertion of worldwide priority.
residual_risks: An earlier paper may have optimized the same two-Hermite radial weighted coverage under a different term.
The known Laguerre formulas make a short proof possible; scientific value is the complete sharp budget law and its quantified noise margin, not the pre-existing ambiguity identity.
The comparison is best-evidence and has not received independent priority review.

value.rationale: Equal-total-budget allocation among the smallest pair of standard Hermite windows is a natural experimentally adjustable conditioning parameter for ambiguity inversion. The theorem gives the exact worst-case design at every disk size and shows a genuine radius transition at \(T=2\). At \(T=4\) the optimized squared margin 0.1126870701 is more than six times the Gaussian-only margin 0.0183156389, and the factor grows as (T-1)^2, so the effect is structural rather than a tiny numerical gain.
